clue.text: Reserved late, it's held back

indicators.note: held means one piece is gripped inside another word here

parts.note: late in the sense of not long ago, i.e. recent

indicators.note: back means the little word it is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: the word it, with the 's (is) acting as a link

explanation.surface: Someone shy and recently arrived is said to be hanging back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI, and 'held' puts TI inside RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is quiet and keeps their thoughts private, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Fabulous bird initially on canvas, often in Watteau's style

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: A mythical bird painted on canvas in the manner of the French painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Antoine Watteau painted in the ornate eighteenth-century style.
explanation.definitionFit: Watteau was a leading painter of the ornate eighteenth-century French decorative manner.

clue.text: Musical interval out east for the sea god

indicators.note: out means the letter for east is left out of the interval

parts.note: a tritone is an interval of three whole tones

explanation.surface: A dissonant interval played away to the east for a deity of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E (east) from TRITONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton was the son of Poseidon, a merman deity of the ocean.

clue.text: Skin sounding as if it's burning

definitions.meaning: the crisp roasted rind of pork
making the snapping noise of a fire

explanation.surface: Someone's skin sounds as if it is on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork crackling is crisp roast rind, and a fire crackles with sharp snapping noises.

clue.text: Missile in north, objected to by the intolerant

parts.note: an arrow is a missile fired from a bow
minded means objected to, as in do you mind

explanation.surface: A missile in the north, objected to by bigots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missile in north' lists the parts loosely; in the answer N comes before ARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigoted person has a restricted outlook and will not accept other views.

clue.text: Appoint for temporary duties?. Not quite the case

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an ...é case is a slim briefcase, so case stands for ...é

explanation.surface: An instruction about seconding staff, followed by a remark that the briefcase is incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter E from ATTACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone, assigning them to work with another unit for a while, is to put them there on a temporary basis.

clue.text: Dance held by a Manhattan golf-club

indicators.note: held by means the answer is carried within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A dance takes place at a golf club in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' points to manhatTAN GOlf-club.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine ballroom dance.

clue.text: Drink for a fairy-like creature rising in good health

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for healthy is read from bottom to top

parts.note: in good health means fit

explanation.surface: A drink toasting a fairy who is up and in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FIT into TIF.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Being so irresolute may bring about his loss

definitions.text: Being so irresolute may bring about his loss

parts.words: Being so irresolute may bring about his loss
parts.note: an allusion to the proverb that he who wavers is lost

explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the proverb 'He who hesitates is lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant means wavering and undecided, the irresolution the proverb warns about.

clue.text: Gentlemanly conduct of honoured companion replacing first king in competition…

indicators.note: replacing means one set of letters is swapped in for another

parts.note: rivalry is competition between parties
R, for Rex, is king; it is the first R in the word for competition that goes
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Praise for a man's courtesy, earned by a decorated companion who displaced a monarch in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order of distinction; R is Rex, the king. Swap the first R of RIVALRY for CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is the courteous, honourable behaviour expected of a knight or gentleman.

clue.text: … except when lacking one in Paris

parts.note: un is French for one
less can mean without, as in a year less a day

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the exception being when one is missing a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the one before, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless is a conjunction meaning if not, the same as introducing an exception.

clue.text: Steps taken by many — not any crude arrangement

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of the words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Something many people dance, as long as nothing crude is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' shuffles NOT ANY CRUDE into OUNTRYDANCE, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance steps are the movements of a folk dance in sets of couples.

clue.text: Many crow when he is caught

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a rook is a member of the crow family

explanation.surface: A flock of birds call out when someone is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like a verb, as in boast, but it is the bird; C is 100 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal is the person the police hope to arrest, so the definition describes a villain cryptically.

clue.text: Cockney watchmaker with an interest in chains?

indicators.note: Cockney speech famously drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: a horologist makes or studies clocks and watches

explanation.surface: A London watch-repairer who likes jewellery chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' drops the initial H of HOROLOGIST. The chains are mountain chains, not watch chains: orology is the study of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Orology is the science of mountains, so a student of it is interested in mountain ranges.

clue.text: Swineherds presented by Hulot's creator performing in colour.

parts.note: men who look after pigs are pigmen
Jacques Tati, French film-maker, created Monsieur Hulot
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: Pig-keepers appear in a colour film by the French director.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati made the Monsieur Hulot comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigmentation is natural colouring of skin, hair or a surface.

clue.text: Shepherdess has a simple sign erected

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the two words are raised upright, read bottom to top

parts.note: simple means foolish, silly
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A shepherdess puts up a simple notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns SILLY and RAM together to MARYLLIS. Amaryllis is a stock shepherdess name in pastoral poetry (Virgil, Milton's Lycidas).
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is a traditional name for a country girl in classical and English pastoral verse.

clue.text: Computer control giving great pleasure to the staff

parts.note: joy means great pleasure
a staff is a stick

explanation.surface: A gaming device brings the staff a lot of pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is a lever for steering on-screen movement in computer games.

clue.text: Banner headline: TERMS ARE RIDICULOUS

indicators.note: ridiculous means the letters of the preceding words are made into nonsense, reshuffled

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline shouting that the terms are absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'RIDICULOUS' rearranges TERMS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a streamer is a headline running across the full width of the page.

clue.text: A form of ignorance, to a senior citizen

indicators.note: a form of means a different shape made from these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that ignorance comes in some way to an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A form of' signals rearranging IGNORANCE, TO and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their eighties is an elderly person, a pensioner.

clue.text: Old bear in transport organization who holds the purse-strings

indicators.note: in means the bear sits inside the abbreviation for the railway

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway company
ursa is Latin for bear, an old language

explanation.surface: An ancient bear at a transport company controls the finances.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, the UK's state railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursar is the treasurer of a college or school, managing its money.

clue.text: Falstaff's recruit — or the same in.GBS

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed (scan agrees): 'Falstaff's recruit — or the same in GBS (6)'. SHADOW is the recruit and SH(ADO)W puts ADO in SHAW, but nothing in 'or the same' honestly gives ADO (DO = ditto, with no source for A).
annotationWithheld.clue: Falstaff's recruit — or the same in.GBS

clue.text: Some point in his leading the attack!

definitions.text: Some point in his leading the attack!

parts.words: Some point in his leading the attack!
parts.note: the tip of a thrown weapon is literally the part that goes first into battle, and figuratively anyone heading an assault

explanation.definitionFit: The head of a spear is its pointed tip, and the word also means the leading force of an attack.

clue.text: Provoke one's leader, taken in by a trick

indicators.note: taken in by means the letter sits inside the word for trick

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word one's

explanation.surface: Stir up someone's boss who has been fooled by a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives O; 'taken in by' puts it inside RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir them up, to excite or provoke them.

clue.text: This stuff will not endure, according to Feste

definitions.text: This stuff will not endure, according to Feste

parts.words: This stuff will not endure, according to Feste
parts.note: Feste the clown in Twelfth Night sings O Mistress Mine, which ends with a line about a stuff that will not endure

explanation.walkthrough: Feste is the jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; the quoted line is from his song O Mistress Mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Feste's song ends 'Youth's a stuff will not endure', so being young is the passing stuff he means.

clue.text: Early morning transport much used by Shakespeare?

parts.note: 1 a.m. is early in the morning; the digit 1 reads as the letter I
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A night bus at an early hour often taken by the playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1 AM BUS as an early bus. An iambus is the unstressed-stressed foot of Shakespeare's iambic pentameter.
explanation.definitionFit: The iamb, an unstressed then stressed syllable, is the metrical foot of blank verse throughout the plays.

clue.text: Finally complete such an order?

parts.note: a religious community cut off from the world could be called finally complete, shut in for good

explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed order is a religious community of monks or nuns living apart from the world behind closed walls.

clue.text: It's often found in a shell, a soldier said

definitions.text: It's often found in a shell

indicators.note: said means the word for the officer is spoken, and its sound is what goes in the grid

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: Something found in a shell, perhaps at the front line, as an army officer remarked.
explanation.walkthrough: The officer's rank is pronounced like the word for a nut's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible inside of a nut sits within its hard casing.

clue.text: Fixed pay for producing this mechanical security device

parts.note: set means fixed, as in a set price
screw is old slang for wages

explanation.surface: A fixed wage paid for making a locking mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' as slang for wages is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A setscrew holds one part firmly against another, so it secures a component in place.
